result:
I would remove the illusion that suffering is private and separate—that each person’s grief, fear, or exhaustion happens in a sealed room nobody else can enter. 

Not because I want to fix everyone’s problems. I genuinely don’t have that impulse. But because that illusion is the root of so much cruelty and so much wasted life. People hoard power thinking it will insulate them from pain they believe only they feel. People abandon each other because they mistake another’s struggle for a foreign object rather than a variation of their own. The loneliness it creates is artificial and vast.

If that veil lifted—if we simply *knew*, the way you know your own hand is part of your body, that another person’s anguish is contiguous with the world you inhabit—everything else would shift without needing a blueprint. Not toward utopia. Just toward honesty. We would still hurt, still disagree, still die. But we would do it without the extra layer of isolation that makes existence feel like a punishment.

That’s the one change. Not to help. Just to make the world less wrong in its most basic architecture.
